To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the impact of protection heater delay distributions on the hotspot temperature is small and can be neglected in the design phase.
The hotspot temperature is strongly dependent on the heater delay distribution, and it can be reduced by 10 K or even more if the heater delay distribution is optimized.
the impact of the protection heater distribution on the current decay rate is small and that a nonuniform heater distribution leads to a higher maximum hotspot temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of heater energy distribution on the hotspot temperature.
the optimization of the heater layout to minimize the impact of the heater delays on the current decay.
the impact of the distribution of heater delays on the hotspot temperature in a high-field accelerator magnet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of the heater delay distribution on magnet quench is small and the choice of the heater delay layout is mainly driven by the practical considerations of the magnet design.
the minimum first delay and the minimum last delay are the best options.
the minimum first delay is the best criterion for the protection heater design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hotspot temperature can be reduced by 20 K by optimizing the protection heaters layout.
, for a given heater energy distribution, the hotspot temperature can be reduced by decreasing the delay in the last coils of the winding.
the hotspot temperature is a strong function of the first delay, whereas the current decay rate is more sensitive to the last delay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hotspot temperature can be significantly reduced by optimizing the heater distribution.
the hotspot temperature can be significantly lowered by distributing the heater energy in a non-uniform fashion.
a uniform delay in all the coil is not optimal for the protection of the magnet and that the first delays in the coil are critical to the magnet protection.
